messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: data-plane p99 latency > 1.2s for /v1/generate (streaming=true) across us-west-2. Error rate rising, autoscaler not keeping up. Pager sent to @maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing token/sec drop and queue growth on model pool-a. initiating triage.

liam: Which dimension is saturated? GPU mem, CPU, or network?

maya (oncall): GPU utilization ~95% on 3 nodes, KV cache eviction rate up, mux queue length spiking. tail logs show a lot of long-lived SSE connections holding resources.

ops-eng: This matches the upstream burst pattern we saw in the canary last week. Streaming keeps long-lived connections and prevents quick reclamation of capacity.

sara: Customer impact? Any degraded non-streaming routes?

maya (oncall): Non-streaming generative calls (polling) still fine for most customers, but streaming customers see delayed first-token and timeouts. A few PLG apps reported UI hang.

ben: Recommendation: temporarily disable streaming responses globally for hosted tier (toggle to non-streaming fallback) so active long-lived SSEs are terminated and capacity freed. Doable via feature-flag in the control plane: `feature.streaming_responses.enabled = false` for hosted-prod. Can roll back quickly.

liam: Need pager approval + clear rollback plan. How long to flip?

maya (oncall): If we agree, I can flip feature flag now and push a controlled disabling window with gradual gating. Steps below.

ops-eng: Runbook items:
1) Set `feature.streaming_responses.enabled=false` for env=hosted-prod (control plane).
2) Shift routing policy: route streaming requests to non-streaming handler with `X-Stream-Fallback: true`.
3) Increase short-term quotas for poll endpoints to absorb load.
4) Monitor p99 latency, token/sec, SSE connection count.
5) Notify support and customers.

maya (oncall): Executing step 1 now.

maya (oncall): `curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/flags/streaming_responses" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"enabled":false,"reason":"live mitigation - stabilize p99"}'`

deploy-bot: Feature flag streaming_responses set to false by maya. Toggle ID: ff-2026-08-15-07. Rolling propagation across regions.

maya (oncall): Propagation to us-west-2 complete. Kicking off graceful connection drain for SSE muxes.

liam: Observing metrics... p99 falls from 1.25s -> 650ms within ~90s. Connection count down 78%. Good.

ops-eng: Error rate for non-streaming stable. Some client-side UIs might retry; watch 429s.

sara: Notifying support + customers now. PR template: short blurb + expected behavior + ETA for re-enable.

customers-team: Message posted to status page and key accounts. We'll route urgent tickets to on-call.

ben: For safety, we should also apply a temporary per-route rate limit to aggressively-shaped streaming proxies to avoid request storms after clients fallback to polling. Applying 100 rps per IP for /v1/generate-poll for next 15m.

maya (oncall): Rate limits applied.

liam: Observed backlog draining and model cpu/gpu headroom increasing. p95/p99 stable now. Good signal.

ops-eng: Timeline proposal: keep streaming disabled for an initial 30-minute stabilization window, then run a controlled canary re-enable with a small % of traffic and close monitoring.

maya (oncall): +1. We'll set circuit-breaker: if p99 > 900ms or error-rate increases > 2x baseline, auto flip off and rollback to non-streaming.

ben: Who owns post-incident? I can take postmortem and action items: identify cause (connection churn + long-lived requests), propose longer-term mitigations (idle-kill thresholds, improved muxing, backpressure in agent libs), and plan a staged re-enable with client-side guidance.

sara: I'll coordinate customer comms and include affected accounts list.

customers-team: Support is on standby and we've prepared canned responses.

maya (oncall): Starting 30m stabilization timer. Will walk handoff in 20m to next oncall if still needed.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0815-01 (streaming-fallback-mitigation). Severity: P2. Linked runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-mitigation.

deploy-bot: Canary re-enable plan ready. Steps to re-enable:
- Flip `feature.streaming_responses.enabled=true` for 1% traffic in us-west-2
- Monitor p99, error-rate, connection churn for 10 minutes
- Gradually increase to 10% if stable, then 100%

liam: I'll prepare the canary policy and watch dashboards.

maya (oncall): Handing off after 20m to liam if stable. Otherwise I'll stay.

ben: Postmortem owner assigned: ben. Target draft within 72 hours.

maya (oncall): Final note: keep an eye on dedicated/private customers — their streaming settings are separate; we didn't flip anything there. Contact me if there's spillover. :white_check_mark:
